<h1 align="center">Castaway <sup>+10</sup></h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>A ten-hour lo-fi island video with ten options. All ten are locked, on purpose.</b><br>
  <sub>working title · in development, nothing published yet · an unofficial remake inspired by the 1992 screensaver <i>Johnny Castaway</i></sub>
</p>

**Castaway** is a stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, in the spirit of the ten-hour streams: a young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft and a lot of time. She mostly idles, nodding to the music in her headphones, and every so often, always on the next bar of the music, something happens. A bottle she throws washes straight back. A drone delivers a parcel, and the parcel is more headphones. A shark surfaces in headphones and nods along. Sunny, hand-painted coastal anime, 16:9, 1080p at 30 fps, and always daytime.

Four timers and more than 90 activities decide what happens and when, and every sound in it is synthesized from code: no samples, no loops, no recordings. The menu up there cannot change any of that. Nobody can. It is a feature.

```sh
python tools/serve.py        # then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

<sub>Live preview, and export to a YouTube-ready MP4: the browser encodes frame-exact H.264 and the server mixes in the sound. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm packages.</sub>

<pre>
            ATOLL ORDER presents CASTAWAY +7: the keys that do work

  F1  <a href="tools/serve.py">START THE ISLAND</a> ............................... python tools/serve.py
  F2  <a href="web/index.html">WATCH LIVE, EXPORT THE MP4</a> .................... http://127.0.0.1:8765/
  F3  <a href="tools/schedule.py">SIMULATE TEN HOURS OF IT</a> .................... python tools/schedule.py
  F4  <a href="tools/make_audio.py">SYNTHESIZE EVERY SOUND</a> .................... python tools/make_audio.py
  F5  <a href="tools/render_demo.py">DEV REEL, ONE OF EVERYTHING</a> ........ python tools/render_demo.py --dev
  F6  <a href="activities.toml">READ THE TIMERS</a> ...................................... activities.toml
  F7  <a href="MUSING.md">READ THE LOG</a> ............................................... MUSING.md

  ENTER: F1, then F2.     ESC: see F9 in the picture.     F8 to F10: locked.
</pre>

<details>
<summary><b>OPTIONS.TXT</b>: why all ten options are locked</summary>

<br>

| Key | Option | State | Why it will not budge |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| F1 | Unlimited daylight | `ON` | Always daytime. It is a project rule, not a setting: no night scenes, ever. |
| F2 | Something happens | `SOON-ISH` | Four timers: regular every 2 to 5 minutes, occasional every 12 to 25, rare every 30 to 60, super rare every 3 to 6 hours (three at most per run). |
| F3 | Ship notices her | `OFF` | Lanes let things overlap, so a ship can cross the horizon while she is busy with a coconut. It even waits for her to get busy. Headphones. It sails on. |
| F4 | Samples and loops | `NONE` | More than 150 sound files, every one synthesized from code by [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py). |
| F5 | Gags land on the beat | `ON` | Every activity starts on the next bar of the music, and a bar is exactly 3 seconds. |
| F6 | Phone signal | `1 BAR` | The signal hunt ends at the very top of the palm, with one bar. |
| F7 | Headphone delivery | `BY DRONE` | A drone lowers a parcel. Inside: another pair of headphones. Later a wave lifts the empty box and floats it off to sea. |
| F8 | Bottle stays away | `OFF` | Her message in a bottle washes straight back. Much later, a different bottle brings a reply. |
| F9 | Leave the island | `ANY TIME` | Super rare: she walks out over the water and comes back with an iced coffee. Never explained. |
| F10 | Random seed | `1992` | The default run is 10:00:00 on seed 1992: same seed, same ten hours, bar for bar. |

In the banner the cursor rests on each option for two bars (6 seconds), so it goes round all ten once per loop of the 60-second theme. The key goes down on beat three, the state flips for one beat, and it flips back. F9 is the exception: it holds while she is gone.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>TIMERS.TXT</b>: how long you wait, and for what</summary>

```text
  TIMERS.TXT                       activities.toml, as of 2026-10-01

  93 activities: 81 on the four timers, 12 chained follow-ups
  counts are the median of 200 simulated 10-hour runs

  [REGULAR]     every 2 to 5 minutes ..................... about 155 a run
                a coconut in the shade, fishing (nothing bites), jogging
                laps, a sandcastle
  [OCCASIONAL]  every 12 to 25 minutes .................... about 30 a run
                the ship that sails past, the bottle that comes back, the
                sea turtle, the coconut that lands on a hermit crab (who
                walks off wearing it), planting a kumara
  [RARE]        every 30 to 60 minutes .................... about 13 a run
                the drone, the signal hunt, the cat on a crate, the shark
                in headphones, the tour boat of selfie-takers, the
                hydrofoil bro (one shaka, then he carves off), fire by
                friction, a hammock, a lookout up the palm, spear fishing
  [SUPER RARE]  every 3 to 6 hours, 3 at most .............. about 2 a run
                she could leave any time; she waves for rescue
  [CHAINED]     only after something else ............... as they come due
                the tide takes the sandcastle, a reply in a different
                bottle, the kumara she planted grows over the video
  [IDLE]        the rest of the time ................... about two thirds
                nodding. on the beat.
```

Every start snaps to the next bar of the music, every 3 seconds, so every punchline lands on the beat. She is busy for about a third of a run. The default run is 10:00:00 with seed 1992, and `python tools/schedule.py` checks the file and simulates one. Scene life has 26 entries of its own: shore waves and drifting cloud shadows are built; distant birds, planes with vapour trails, whale pods, dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko and a rain shower are planned.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>SOUND.TXT</b>: every noise, from arithmetic</summary>

```text
  SOUND.TXT                                  made by tools/make_audio.py

  samples ............................................................. 0
  loops borrowed ...................................................... 0
  recordings .......................................................... 0
  third-party licences ................................................ 0
  sound files written .................. more than 150, and still growing
  theme ............. a seamless 60 s loop at 80 BPM in F major (ii-V-I-vi)
                      20 bars of exactly 3 s
  instruments ....... electric piano, kalimba lead, soft drums, vinyl crackle
  ocean ............. a seamless 60 s loop of its own
  mix ............... -14 LUFS, true peak at or below -1 dBTP
  levels ............ adjustable, in master and per routine
  listened to ......................................... not yet, by anybody
```

The level meters in the banner are drawn, not measured: they kick on beats one and three and snap on two and four, at the theme's 80 BPM. Nobody has heard the real thing yet, so this page has no opinion about how it sounds.

</details>
